problem: Which of the following is a schematic of the Cartesian product $A\times B$ for $A={p,q}$ and $B={w,z}?$

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/d6ee87bd861491394c6643679f62cb4b94436bf2777bd2436b3169e779736e2c.png)

Using the visual schematic above for the Cartesian product ${A}^{2}$ for $A={h,k},$ determine which of the following statements are true.

- ${h}^{2}\in {A}^{2}$
- $(h,k)\in {A}^{2}$
- $(k,k)\in {A}^{2}$
feedback.worked_solution:
The set ${A}^{2}$ is equivalent to the Cartesian product $A\times A.$

The Cartesian product $A\times B$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $A$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $B.$

To complete our schematic of $A\times A,$ we write an ordered pair whose first coordinate is the corresponding element of the first set $(A)$ and the second coordinate is the corresponding element of the second set $(A)$ at each intersection.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072443/assets/507f8f6306c309d5e894cfb1dabfc2019f371911f7878b196e1f329f1b37dfa6.png)

According to our diagram:

- ${h}^{2}\in {A}^{2}\,\times $

- $(h,k)\in {A}^{2}\,✓$

- $(k,k)\in {A}^{2}\,✓$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
